source.view: sina quoted tape + the session's published unit NAV (fallback: the IOPV board did not answer)
source.denominator: the session's published unit NAV, NOT an intraday IOPV
source.nav_board: same-day unit NAV board (fund_etf_fund_daily_em) used as the second source

cross_check.basis: premium recomputed from price/IOPV; the board's own 折价率 column is only compared

over_hurdle.basis: sum over priced legs only; unverified legs carry no CNY figure and are excluded, never counted as zero. A priced leg whose date is only a label adds at most |its own move| x amount to the sum -- that move is the largest difference the two candidate NAV days can carry -- so the gate certifies a saving only when even that worst case stays under the threshold.

denominator_rebasis.basis: a leg whose own denominator date is not this session is re-priced on the session's published unit NAV when the NAV board carries one; the board's own reading stays in board_reading. With no same-day NAV the leg is nav-cross-date: it keeps the percentage the board printed, carries no CNY, and never claims to be this session's premium.

denominator.basis: each row carries the date its own denominator belongs to; never inferred

date_evidence.basis: a batch stamp says which day the snapshot was fetched; the dating face says which day each instrument's denominator belongs to, from the move that instrument made. Where the two disagree the path wins and the leg is priced as cross-date; where the path cannot tell (|move| under its threshold) the leg keeps its number and is marked label-only with the ambiguity printed. A leg those two statements put in different sessions is re-priced on the NAV this session published -- its day is then decided by that repricing, so it stays on the label-only roster (how the original date was known) and off the gate's bill.

caveats: IOPV is a real-time estimate of the basket, not the fund's published NAV; a premium measured against it inherits that error.
the spot board publishes 折价率 (discount), the opposite sign of a premium -- this face recomputes from price/IOPV and reports any disagreement instead of choosing a side.

a cross-border leg publishes its NAV at T+n, so on the session itself its IOPV cannot be checked against anything. Those legs are marked unverified and carry NO CNY figure: an IOPV that has drifted from the basket looks exactly like a real premium from one snapshot.
the board is read at one moment: before the close these numbers move, and cross-border legs are the ones that move most (their underlying trades in another timezone).
a positive premium is a cost only to a buyer; it is income to a seller. This face says nothing about which side the book will be on tomorrow.

no historical premium series is long enough to build a percentile gate from: this face runs once per session on the daily chain from 2026-11-06, so a 'is today's premium high for this leg' reading has to wait for the series to accumulate.

this session's denominator is the fund's published unit NAV, not an intraday IOPV: the premium is measured against the day's official net asset value, so it carries no intraday basket drift -- and it is only coarsely comparable with an IOPV-based premium from an earlier session.
